Someone Offered $347,000 for This 2027 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X and Somehow That Still Wasn't Enough
20 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
Now, before we start feeling sorry for the seller, let's crunch some numbers. This particular ZR1X Convertible packs an original sticker price of $295,000, which means the highest bidder was willing to pay $52,000 over MSRP. Unfortunately for them, the seller, a dealer out of California, had a higher number in mind.
But is $347,000 (plus a buyer's fee) a reasonable offer? I'd say so - despite the fact that we've already seen other dealers dumping their ZR1X Convertibles for three figures over sticker. So yeah, there's plenty of money to be made on these things, assuming you can find the right buyer.
I've also noticed that people have been trying to get prices to go down on the ZR1X at auction, and all it takes is one seller to bite and that pretty much shifts the market instantly, whether other sellers like it or not. Still, how much more could this car have fetched? Are we talking $360,000? Maybe $375,000? I'm genuinely not sure why you would pay such a premium at this point in time. But I guess it depends on how badly you want the car, and whether or not it's a delivery miles example.
This one here certainly is, with just 4 miles on the odometer. It also comes with a Blade Silver Metallic exterior, which I really like.
I think this is one of my favorite C8 colors, to be honest. And it works really well together with the asymmetrical Edge Red and Carbon Flash racing stripes - not to mention the carbon fiber mirror caps, a carbon fiber rear wing, tall hood spoiler, front dive planes, LED headlights and the carbon fiber accents for the power-retractable hardtop. If you like carbon fiber, there's plenty of it to go around on this car. Let's just say that.
The 20" and 21" wheels are also carbon fiber and are wrapped in Michelin rubber while housing carbon-ceramic discs and the optional Edge Red-painted calipers. The car does come with the ZTK Performance suspension courtesy of the Performance Track Package , and there's a front-axle lift system for good measure. The latter is an absolute must-have on a ZR1X, especially with such a track-focused spec. Not that you'd want to take this car out on track if you're a collector.
Photo: Bring a Trailer We can't mention the interior without discussing the asymmetrical upholstery. The left-side heated and ventilated GT2 bucket seats are trimmed in Adrenaline Red leather with black accents, while the right-side seat features Jet Black leather.
Furthermore, contrast stitching can be found throughout the cabin. Other highlights include the Stealth Interior Trim Package, a performance data and video recorder, a 14-speaker Bose Performance Series sound system, wireless charging, a head-up display, and plenty more.
As for performance, it all comes down to the mid-mounted twin-turbo 5.5-liter LT7 V8 engine, working alongside an electric motor and a 1.9-kWh battery pack. Together, they produce 1,250 horsepower and 973 lb-ft (1,320 Nm) of torque, with everything hitting all four wheels via an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic and an electronic all-wheel drive system.
